messages:
matt: Heads up — eu-west3 GPU provisioning is blocked. Multiple scratchpool nodes report sudden NVMe 'hotblock' wear spikes and a backlog of ephemeral cleanup tasks, causing attach failures for new GPU pods. Anyone seeing similar?

opsbot: [ALERT] nvme.wear_rate spike on node g-eu-43 (metric: nvme.wear_pct) at 2026-03-19T22:04:11Z. Affected: 6/24 ephemeral devices. See /ops/alerts/5492

sophia: seeing it. grab logs now, looks like scrub jobs and janitor overlap causing write amplification on a small subset of devices.

raj: can you paste the scrub/crond config? last change to janitor window was yesterday during the batch rollout.

lee: quick note — this is localized to a handful of gnode series with older firmware. Wear-leveling counters show uneven block hotness, not whole-disk wear.

matt: interesting. logs: ```
[2026-03-19T21:59:02Z] scrub: start /dev/nvme0n1p1
[2026-03-19T22:01:12Z] janitor: cleanup tmpfiles (heavy)
[2026-03-19T22:03:07Z] nvme: hw write queue depth spike -> retry
[2026-03-19T22:04:11Z] nvme: wear_pct 86 -> 93 (hotblocks)
```

sophia: that overlap looks like it lines up. scrub and janitor both hitting same sections after dataset shuffle from recent training runs. we should throttle janitor or shift scrub window.

raj: agree. short term mitigation: 1) mark affected nodes as unschedulable for GPU attaches, 2) re-run janitor with --backoff 2x, 3) trigger targeted scrub reschedule with lower concurrency. I can run commands.

lee: long term: rebalancer needs heuristics to avoid repeated hits on same LBA ranges (hotspot-aware GC). also file system-level wear hints would help — open issue in infra runtime.

matt: cost impact: holding off provisioning adds latency to queued jobs and increases fallback to on-demand dedicated capacity in other regions. I estimate ~3k USD/day if this lasts >12h due to cross-region reroutes.

opsbot: Incident workflow created: INC-2026-0319-nvme-hotblocks; assigned to @raj; priority P2.

raj: I'll execute the mitigation now: mark 6 nodes cordoned, reduce janitor concurrency, and schedule scrubs spaced by 10m. posting commands: ```
kubectl cordon g-eu-43 g-eu-44 g-eu-46
opsctl janitor run --nodes g-eu-43 --concurrency 1 --backoff 120
opsctl scrub schedule --node g-eu-43 --delay 600 --concurrency 1
```

matt: thanks. after that let's run a quick attach smoke test and then uncordon one node at a time.

lee: filing infra-runtime ticket for hotspot-aware rebalancer and firmware upgrade plan. tagging storage-research for modeling wear.

sophia: noted. will monitor nvme.wear_pct, io_wait, and attach_fail metrics and post graphs in INC-2026 thread. :thumbsup:

matt: everyone added as watchers. update here when done.
